name: por-brownout
description: Full-assembly qualifying-brownout re-assertion check of design/netlist/temp_por_top.spice: cold start to a settled released state, a 1.0 V / 50 us dip (5x T_dip,min, well above the deglitch dwell), rail recovery, and confirmation that RESETn re-asserts during the dip and regenerates a full >=1 ms reset pulse before releasing again. Also carries the full-assembly confirmation of #12's single-cell por-reset-pulse minimum and por-reset-valid-floor results.
claim: spec/target-spec.md#por-brownout -- a dip below VPOR-downarrow,min (2.22 V) lasting >= T_dip,min (10 us) must re-assert RESETn and regenerate the full spec/target-spec.md#por-reset-pulse, on the full four-cell assembly with bias_core's real (starved, corner-dependent) recovery dynamics in the loop. Also substantiates spec/target-spec.md#por-reset-pulse (the >=1 ms minimum, and the observed maximum the ratified row asks #14 to record) and spec/target-spec.md#por-reset-valid-floor (valid-low RESETn at a 1.0 V rail) at full-assembly level, both of which #12 previously measured only at the single-cell level. Deterministic corners only (design.ngspice sets sw_stat_mismatch=0); mismatch is #15's job.
analyses: meas tran vrst_pre find v(resetn) at=19.9m
meas tran vdd_dip find v(vdd) at=20.03m
meas tran vrst_dip find v(resetn) at=20.03m
meas tran treassert when v(resetn)=0.3 fall=1 td=20m
meas tran trel2 when v(resetn)=1.0 rise=1 td=20.052m
meas tran trel2_last when v(resetn)=1.0 rise=last td=20.052m
meas tran vrst_final find v(resetn) at=54.5m

resetn_pre_dip_v.description: sanity: RESETn is released (driven high) before the dip starts -- confirms the deck reaches the state the brownout claim is defined against.

vdd_dip_v.description: sanity: the dip actually reached its programmed depth (1.0 V, below VPOR-downarrow,min = 2.22 V at every corner) -- testbench-integrity check, not the spec claim itself.

t_reassert_us.description: THE QUALIFYING-DIP CHECK: RESETn must re-assert (fall below 0.3 V) during or immediately after the 50 us qualifying dip, at every corner. A dip this deep and this long (5x T_dip,min, well above sim/por-output-chain-deglitch/'s 1.86-8.88 us cell-level dwell) must not be filtered out.

t_pulse_regen_ms.description: spec/target-spec.md#por-reset-pulse's >=1 ms minimum, regenerated in the brownout-recovery context and measured on the FULL ASSEMBLY (#12 measured it on por_output_chain alone, 4.21535-7.75209 ms with idealised bias): from the instant RESETn re-asserts (during the dip) to the instant it releases again (after recovery) must be >=1 ms at every corner. This is both the 'full reset pulse is regenerated' half of the por-brownout claim and the observed-maximum recording the por-reset-pulse row asks #14 for -- the run's own max column IS that number, which is why no maximum bound is imposed here (wave 1 ratifies none).

resetn_floor_in_dip_mv.description: spec/target-spec.md#por-reset-valid-floor at full-assembly level: valid-low := V(RESETn) <= min(0.1*VDD, 0.3 V), which at the dip's 1.0 V rail is 100 mV. #12 measured this on por_output_chain alone against a slow rail ramp (1.699 mV absolute worst at ss/-40C, 0.548 % ratio worst at sf/+125C); this is the same claim re-read on the assembled block, in the state a real brownout puts it in.

release_chatter_us.description: no double pulse on the recovery release edge (first vs. last rising crossing).

resetn_final_v.description: RESETn is back to a solid released high by the end of the run, into the 5 pF load -- confirms recovery completed cleanly rather than leaving the block stuck asserted.
